name: Tennessee

sales.rateNote: 7% state rate on most goods and taxable services; food and food ingredients are taxed at a reduced 4% state rate. Counties and some cities add a local rate of up to 2.75%, applied only to the first $1,600 of a single article; a state single article tax of 2.75% applies to the part between $1,600 and $3,200.

local.levies: counties and some incorporated cities (local option sales tax)
local.capNote: Local rates cannot exceed 2.75%, and apply only to the first $1,600 of the price of a single article.

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients are taxed at a reduced 4% state rate plus the full local rate. Prepared food, candy, dietary supplements, alcohol and tobacco pay the general 7% rate.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable except during the July sales tax holiday ($100 or less per item).

otherRates.item: single article state tax (portion of price from $1,600 to $3,200)
otherRates.note: Added state tax on the part of a single item's price above $1,600 up to $3,200, replacing the local tax on that portion.

otherRates.item: digital videos, books and music (local use tax)
otherRates.note: Fixed local rate of 2.5% on these specified digital products regardless of location.

holidays2026.name: Sales tax holiday
holidays2026.items: clothing $100 or less per item; school and school art supplies $100 or less per item; computers $1,500 or less per item

sales.holidayNote: By law the holiday runs from 12:01 a.m. on the last Friday in July to 11:59 p.m. the following Sunday; in 2026 that is July 31 to August 2 (dates computed from the rule).

useTax.note: Use tax at the same rate as sales tax: 7% state (4% on food) plus the local rate, on the purchase price including delivery charges.

facts.text: On a big-ticket item, local tax stops at the first $1,600 of the price, and a 2.75% state single article tax applies only to the next $1,600 (up to $3,200).
Groceries are not exempt: they pay a 4% state rate plus the full local rate.
During the holiday, an item priced above $100 (or $1,500 for a computer) is taxed on its entire price: there is no partial exemption.
Over-the-counter drugs are taxable unless bought with a prescription.
Prepared food is taxed at the general 7% state rate plus local tax, not the 4% food rate.

property.levied: local (counties and cities set rates; county assessors appraise; county trustees collect)

assessment.text: Assessed value is a fixed share of appraised value set by state law: 25% for residential and farm property, 40% for commercial and industrial. Rates are per $100 of assessed value. Each county reappraises all real property on a 4, 5 or 6-year cycle.

homestead.name: No general homestead exemption
homestead.text: Tennessee has no general homestead exemption. Help for homeowners comes from the state Tax Relief program (low-income elderly and disabled owners, disabled veterans) and the local option Property Tax Freeze for owners 65+.
homestead.applyBy: Apply with the county trustee; Tax Relief and Tax Freeze deadlines are 35 days after the local delinquency date.

otherRelief.name: Property Tax Relief (elderly and disabled)
otherRelief.text: State-funded credit for owners 65+ or disabled with 2025 income of $38,470 or less; relief is calculated on up to $33,600 of market value (2026 program).

otherRelief.name: Property Tax Relief (disabled veterans)
otherRelief.text: Qualifying disabled veterans or surviving spouses: relief calculated on up to $175,000 of market value, no income limit stated.

otherRelief.name: Property Tax Freeze
otherRelief.text: Local option (adopted county by county or city by city): freezes the tax on the home of owners 65+ whose income is under the county limit set yearly by the Comptroller.

dueDates.text: Taxes become due on the first Monday in October; the last day to pay without interest is the end of February (they are delinquent on March 1).

facts.text: Official example: a house appraised at $400,000 is assessed at $100,000 (25%); at a $2.50 rate per $100, the bill is $2,500.
Commercial and industrial property is assessed at 40% of value versus 25% for homes, so a business pays more on the same value.
The tax freeze was enabled by a 2006 constitutional amendment and the 2007 Property Tax Freeze Act; each county or city decides whether to adopt it.
County boards of equalization meet from June 1 (May 1 in Shelby County) to hear appeals of assessments.
Personal property is revalued every year, while real property is revalued only every 4 to 6 years.
